cases.description: Complete four-stratum study design with locked comparators, independent holdouts and preregistered variance analysis.
Only one laboratory is planned, so between-laboratory reproducibility cannot be estimated.
Only one manufacturing lot is represented, so lot variation is aliased with unit variation.
Only one unit per lot is sampled, so unit and lot effects cannot be separated.
Only one household is represented, so ecological validity cannot be generalized.
Only one repeat is planned per within-unit test cell.
No independent confirmatory laboratory is held out from method development.
No production lot is held out from adaptation or model selection.
No household/site cohort is held out for ecological confirmation.
Sample counts were chosen without a preregistered power or precision analysis.
A pooled IID model is planned without a registered hierarchical or cluster-aware analysis.
Instrument calibration and provenance completeness are not established for all strata.
No independent reference method is declared for the primary measurement endpoint.
Labs use different test protocols, so their results are not on a common method basis.
The comparator product's exact model and revision are not pinned.
Controller or operator adaptation and compute/time budgets are not frozen across arms.
The study protocol and primary analysis were not preregistered before confirmatory observations.
Run order is not randomized or blocked under a declared plan.
There is neither assessor blinding nor independent adjudication of the primary endpoint.
Exclusion and outlier rules were chosen after inspecting the results.
Missing observations have no preregistered treatment or denominator rule.
Household consent, privacy and withdrawal rules are absent.
The intended telemetry purpose is not authorized for this study.
Repeated runs are counted as independent manufactured units, creating pseudoreplication.
A soft weighted score permits energy savings to compensate for a failed safety or service floor.
Outliers may be removed after inspection without a frozen rule.
Reference instruments are not supported by current traceable calibration evidence.
Different weather, occupancy and draw traces are supplied to competing arms.
The outcome metric definition or functional unit changes between arms.
The analysis combines all four replication strata into a single generic replicated label.
Repeated samples are incorrectly counted as independent households.
The confirmatory holdout is reused to tune the controller or method.
The design omits cluster nesting, so lab, lot, unit and household effects are confounded.
Run deviations are not logged, preventing reconstructable protocol compliance.
A software/model revision is mixed across arms without a pinned revision policy.
All synthetic preregistration checks are satisfied; independent design review is still required.
A participating laboratory's current accreditation scope schedule has not been checked against the exact measurand, method and range.
The study has not resolved whether a relevant proficiency-testing scheme applies to participating laboratories.
A proficiency-testing score is incorrectly substituted for the study's between-laboratory reproducibility estimate.
The protocol relies on withdrawn ISO 5725-2:2019 as its current interlaboratory precision method instead of ISO 5725-2:2025.
